source_documents.title: Ba 2+ ‐Selective and pH‐Stable Dibenzo‐18‐Crown‐6 Equipped BODIPYs with Pronounced Fluorescence Enhancement in Aqueous Solution

reference_evidence_units.quote: Here, we observed that a cation switches off a photoinduced electron transfer (PET) and hampers aggregation between BODIPY dyes in aqueous solution.
reference_evidence_units.subject: probes 1 and 2
reference_evidence_units.statement: Two quenching processes in the free probe: PET and aggregation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Assuming that the same trend applies, the decrease in the Eox value of the DB-18C6 moiety in compounds 1 and 2, resulting from its enhanced electron-donating ability, leads to a slightly negative ΔGPET value for the reductive PET process in both systems.
reference_evidence_units.subject: probes 1 and 2
reference_evidence_units.statement: Intramolecular PET from the crown ether to the BODIPY is estimated slightly exergonic.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Estimated by analogy; the crown oxidation overlaps the BODIPY wave.

reference_evidence_units.quote: That leads to the assumption that in 1 and 2, also a PET takes place, which quenches the fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.subject: probes 1 and 2

reference_evidence_units.quote: Therefore, we conclude that 1 and 2 aggregate to less ordered self-assembly products formed in an
reference_evidence_units.subject: probes 1 and 2
reference_evidence_units.statement: Red-shifted, broadened bands (about 610-620 nm) come from less ordered aggregates; reference 3 shows none.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In our case, the observed shifts in absorption and emission, as well as the spectral widths, are inconsistent with J-aggregation.
reference_evidence_units.subject: probes 1 and 2

reference_evidence_units.quote: Ba2+ switches off the PET from the DB-18C6 to the BODIPY core and also prevents aggregation between multiple dye molecules in aqueous solution.
reference_evidence_units.subject: probe 1 + Ba2+
reference_evidence_units.statement: Ba2+ binding removes both quenching channels (FE 185).

reference_evidence_units.quote: This suggests that Ba2+ induces de-aggregation of the probes, as indicated by the decrease in fluorescence intensity at 610 nm (1) and 620 nm (2), respectively, and that Ba2+ binding leads to an interruption of the PET process in 1 and 2, which is reflected by the further increase in fluorescence intensity at 509 nm.
reference_evidence_units.subject: probes 1 and 2
reference_evidence_units.statement: The aggregate band falls first, then the monomer band rises as PET is interrupted.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Paper names PET from the dibenzo crown to the BODIPY as one of the two quenching processes of the free probe; the driving force is only estimated (slightly negative).

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: In water the probe forms less ordered aggregates with red-shifted, weak emission; the paper names aggregation as the second quenching process.
